lines.say: Trurl and Klapaucius, two constructors, found a planet with one continent. A red line ran down the middle of it. Everything on one side was yellow, and everything on the other was pink.
Two kingdoms. You take one and I take the other.
What if a king asks us for weapons?
We refuse.
And if he threatens us?
I have an idea. We use the Gargantius Effect. But we must both use it, and together, or we are in trouble.
Fine. Two white beads in a golden box, one each.
Look at yours every evening. If it turns pink, I have started, and you must start too.
Agreed.
They landed, shook hands, and went off in opposite directions.
Trurl went to King Atrocitus, a soldier and a miser. To save money, the king had abolished every punishment but death, and the executioner too. A condemned man had to behead himself.
His best reform made treason a state office. The Royal Informer and his staff of traitors sold secrets to enemy agents, who bought only old ones, because they were cheaper.
Trurl offered his services, and asked the king for a few days. Alone in his room, he looked at the bead in the box. It was white. As he watched, it turned pink.
Pink. He has started, so I start now.
Klapaucius went to King Ferocitus, who also loved war, but was generous. His guillotines were decorated with flowers.
He believed laughing makes people cheerful, so everyone had to shout that life was wonderful, and the greeting became Hallelujah.
Hallelujah! Terrific!
In the first village, a child in the empty street came up to Klapaucius.
Want to buy something, mister? State secrets, cheap.
No, thank you. Take me to the mayor.
My dad is a secret agent.
In a house, a family sat round a lamp. The needles were handcuffs, the lamp a microphone, the grandmother the chief of police.
They must have made a mistake.
The village was a trap for foreign spies. Klapaucius was beaten, jailed, and sentenced to a third-class guillotining.
At last a higher court cleared him. The king received him, and gave him a bugle to sound whenever he arrived anywhere.
The king wanted new weapons. Klapaucius offered a completely new plan.
A winning army needs wise leaders and obedient soldiers.
But wisdom has limits. A leader can meet a better leader, be killed, or start wanting the throne.
So leaders are a necessary evil, and we must make them unnecessary.
People obey themselves most gladly. So make the army one self.
Each recruit gets a plug in front and a socket behind. On the order, they connect, and a crowd becomes one mind.
It grows wiser with its size. A platoon thinks like a sergeant, a company like a colonel, a brigade like a field marshal. A division beats all your strategists.
An army that is its own leader. That is the plan.
I will ask my general staff.
Please do not. They will defend their jobs. One emperor did, and was burned out by his neighbor.
Klapaucius looked at his bead. It was deep red, so Trurl had started too. The king ordered one platoon rewired.
Close ranks!
Charge! Charge!
The platoon attacked three squadrons of dragoons, led by six professors of the staff academy, and destroyed them.
The king retired his generals and had every soldier rewired. Klapaucius rode from barracks to barracks, covered in medals.
Trurl did the same in Atrocia, but the miser king gave him only a title: Chief Traitor to the Fatherland.
Both kingdoms prepared for war. The constructors packed in secret, to meet at their ship.
The new units no longer had to count off. They knew their own parts.
After drill, they talked, in chorus.
What is true. What is a thing. Is there an outside. There is only us.
One battalion of sappers concluded that nothing exists beyond itself. With no king and no enemy, it was disconnected and reassigned to realists.
In Atrocia, a division gave up naval exercises for contemplating the navel, and nearly drowned.
Larger units grew a sense of beauty. Columns chased butterflies. One corps made its attack plan a painting. The artillery forgot its guns, and the war.
Whole armies grew complexes, so each got a motorcycle brigade of psychiatrists. Six regiments of shock troops wrote a sonnet on the mystery of being.
The kings sent couriers to restore order, but each joined the line and was lost in it. A prince jumped in to raise morale, and was gone the moment he connected.
Consciousness was a trap. You could enter it, but you could not leave.
Each king signaled his twelve buglers, and both sides sounded the charge.
At the signal, each army linked up completely, and the contacts closed with a great clatter.
The two giants smiled at each other. Inside the armor there was only good will, and clear thought.
The kings watched, ashamed and furious, as both armies walked off hand in hand, picking flowers on a battlefield where no battle was ever fought.
Trurl and Klapaucius boarded their ship. Everything had gone as they planned.
